questions.question: Snapshot isolation is a particular type of ______________ scheme.
questions.explanation: It has gained wide acceptance in commercial and open-source systems, including Oracle, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server.

questions.question: Snapshot isolation is used to give
options: A) Transaction a snapshot of the database
B) Database a snapshot of the transaction
C) Database a snapshot of committed values in the transaction
D) Transaction a snapshot of the database and Database a snapshot of committed values in the transaction
questions.explanation: The data values in the snapshot consist only of values written by committed transactions.

questions.question: ARIES uses a ___________ to identify log records, and stores it in database pages.
questions.explanation: LSN is used to identify which operations have been applied to a database page.

questions.question: ARIES supports ___________ operations, which are physical in that the affected page is physically identified, but can be logical within the page.
questions.explanation: The deletion of a record from a page may result in many other records in the page being shifted, if a slotted page structure is used.

questions.question: ______________ is used to minimize unnecessary redos during recovery.
questions.explanation: Dirty pages are those that have been updated in memory, and the disk version is not up-to-date.

questions.question: __________ scheme that records only information about dirty pages and associated information and does not even require of writing dirty pages to disk.
questions.explanation: It flushes dirty pages in the background, continuously, instead of writing them during checkpoints.

questions.question: Whenever an update operation occurs on a page, the operation stores the LSN of its log record in the _______ field of the page.
questions.explanation: Each page maintains an identifier called the PageLSN.

questions.question: There are special redo-only log records generated during transaction rollback, called _________ in ARIES.
questions.explanation: These serve the same purpose as the redo-only log records in our earlier recovery scheme.

questions.question: The __________________ contains a list of pages that have been updated in the database buffer.
questions.explanation: Dirty pages are those that have been updated in memory, and the disk version is not up-to-date.

questions.question: ___________ determines which transactions to undo, which pages were dirty at the time of the crash, and the LSN from which the redo pass should start.
questions.explanation: The analysis pass finds the last complete checkpoint log record, and reads in the DirtyPageTable from this record.

questions.question: __________ starts from a position determined during analysis, and performs a redo, repeating history, to bring the database to a state it was in before the crash.
questions.explanation: The redo pass repeats history by replaying every action that is not already reflected in the page on disk.

questions.question: ______________ rolls back all transactions that were incomplete at the time of crash.
questions.explanation: It performs a single backward scan of the log, undoing all transactions in undo-list.

questions.question: Which lock should be obtained to prevent a concurrent transaction from executing a conflicting read, insert or delete operation on the same key value.
questions.explanation: Operations acquire lower-level locks while they execute, but release them when they complete; the corresponding transaction must however retain a higher-level lock in a two-phase manner to prevent concurrent transactions from executing conflicting actions.

questions.question: Once the lower-level lock is released, the operation cannot be undone by using the old values of updated data items, and must instead be undone by executing a compensating operation; such an operation is called
questions.explanation: It is important that the lower-level locks acquired during an operation are sufficient to perform a subsequent logical undo of the operation.

questions.question: Which of the following is used for undo operations alone?
options: D) Physical logging and Physical log records
questions.explanation: If the operation inserted an entry in a B+-tree, the undo information U would indicate that a deletion operation is to be performed, and would identify the B+-tree and what entry to delete from the tree. Such logging of information about operations is called logical logging.

questions.question: Redo operations are performed exclusively using
options: D) Both Physical logging and Physical log records
questions.explanation: Logging of old-value and new-value information is called physical logging.

questions.question: To perform logical redo or undo, the database state on disk must be operation ___________ that is, it should not have partial effects of any operation.
questions.explanation: Data structures such as B+-trees would not be in a consistent state, and neither logical redo nor logical undo operations can be performed on an inconsistent data structure.

questions.question: An operation is said to be __________ if executing it several times in a row gives the same result as executing it once.
questions.explanation: Operations such as inserting an entry into a B+-tree may not be idempotent, and the recovery algorithm must therefore make sure that an operation that has already been performed is not performed again.

questions.question: The remote backup site is sometimes also called the
questions.explanation: We can achieve high availability by performing transaction processing at one site, called the primary site, and having a remote backup site where all the data from the primary site are replicated.

questions.question: Remote backup system must be _________ with the primary site.
questions.explanation: We can achieve high availability by performing transaction processing at one site, called the primary site, and having a remote backup site where all the data from the primary site are replicated.

questions.question: The backup is taken by
options: C) Sending all log records from primary site to the remote backup site
D) Sending selected records from primary site to the remote backup site
questions.explanation: We can achieve high availability by performing transaction processing at one site, called the primary site, and having a remote backup site where all the data from the primary site are replicated.

questions.question: When the __________ the backup site takes over processing and becomes the primary.
questions.explanation: When the original primary site recovers, it can either play the role of remote backup, or take over the role of primary site again.

questions.question: The simplest way of transferring control is for the old primary to receive __________ from the old backup site.
questions.explanation: If control must be transferred back, the old backup site can pretend to have failed, resulting in the old primary taking over.

questions.question: The time to process the remote backup can be reduced by
questions.explanation: If the log at the remote backup grows large, recovery will take a long time. The remote backup site can periodically process the redo log records that it has received and can perform a checkpoint, so that earlier parts of the log can be deleted.

questions.question: A _______________ configuration can make takeover by the backup site almost instantaneous.
questions.explanation: In this configuration, the remote backup site continually processes redo log records as they arrive, applying the updates locally.

questions.question: A transaction commits as soon as its commit log record is written to stable storage at the primary site. This is
questions.explanation: The problem with this scheme is that the updates of a committed transaction may not have made it to the backup site, when the backup site takes over processing.

questions.question: A transaction commits as soon as its commit log record is written to stable storage at the primary and the backup site. This is
questions.explanation: The problem with this scheme is that transaction processing cannot proceed if either the primary or the backup site is down.

questions.question: If only the primary is active, the transaction is allowed to commit as soon as its commit log record is written to stable storage at the primary site. This is
questions.explanation: This scheme provides better availability than does two-very-safe, while avoiding the problem of lost transactions faced by the one-safe scheme.
